obligations.rationale: JHU grants a non-exclusive license to make and sell products under its active-cannula patents and patent applications, which Virtuoso can use as they exist, and because JHU prosecutes the patents at its sole discretion without changing what the license lets Virtuoso do, it is functional IP transferred when granted.

rationale: Fixed consideration is the $2,000 license fee plus shares equal to 5% of Virtuoso's fully diluted stock, a noncash payment measured at fair value. The 4% running royalty on net sales and net service revenues is a sales-based royalty on a license of IP, so JHU recognizes it only as the sales occur. Judgment call: the $3,000 minimum annual royalties are not locked in, because Virtuoso can terminate on 60 days' notice. The 1% liquidity-event fee is not sales- or usage-based, so it is ordinary variable consideration, estimated and constrained until a sale or IPO is probable.
